RHODE ISLAND MODE EFFECT ANALYSIS OF
 2016 PARCC RESULTS

 Damian W Betebenner
 National Center for the Improvement of Educational Assessment
 Providence, RI July 18th, 2016

RECAP/OVERVIEW

• 2015 NECAP to PARCC SGP analyses were conducted in late 2015/early 2016.

• Based upon reports from the eld that online and paper & pencil forms were not equivalent,
 SGPs were analyzed between the two modes of administration.
• Signi cant mode effects were discovered as part of the SGP analyses where paper and pencil
 test takers generally had an advantage of those taking the online administered test.
• The mode effects were larger in English Language Arts than in Mathematics. Median SGP for
 P&P were often at/above 60 whereas Median SGPs for Online were in mid 40s.
• Pearson analyses con rmed the existence of mode effects.

2016 OVERVIEW

• Dual mode administration was again allowed in Rhode Island

• Students were not required to take the test using the same mode as in 2015. Thus 4
 combinations across two years are possible:
 • 2015 Online/2016 Online
 • 2015 Online/2016 Paper
 • 2015 Paper/2016 Online
 • 2015 Paper/2016 Paper
• We know mode effects exist with prior scores, also possible this year with current scores.
• Currently (to the best of my knowledge) PARCC decided not to pursue a mode adjustment
 but allowed states to work with Pearson to implement a mode adjustment with their data
 (Colorado only state pursuing a mode adjustment — possibly for both years).

2016 OVERVIEW

• Analyses of 2016 PARCC data conducted using preliminary le provided by RIDE.

• SGPs were calculated using scaled scores (not thetas) under two conditions:
 • single prior (only PARCC data)
 • up to 5 priors (including NECAP data)
• SGPs calculated with thetas will demonstrate the same mode effect properties as those
 calculated with scale scores.
• Analyses conducted for Mathematics, Algebra I, Geometry, and English Language Arts

QUESTIONS TO BE ANSWERED TODAY
 • Are we making any mode adjustments that will impact SGPs?
 • If so, for both 2015 and 2016? And how?
 • Individual SGPs – potentially impacts GMV and accountability.
 • Aggregate – could result in discrepancies between aggregates in GMV and accountability.
 • What SGPs will be used in GMV? Current assumption is that we will use the ones that are
 presented in ISRs.
 • Need cutscores for GMV. Should we try to be consistent between GMV and accountability. If
 so, need to nalize cuts very soon.
 • Current GMV cuts are:
 • High: 71-99
 • High typical: 56-70
 • Typical: 46-55
 • Low typical 31-45
 • Low: 1-30

SUMMARY

 • Signi cant mode effects persist in 2016 data.
 • Given the permutations of different modes across 2 years, dif cult to tease out.
 • Because of small N size in some groups, impossible to just run separate SGP analyses for
 each group.
 • If mode adjustments are desired two possibilities
 • Adjust scale scores for both 2015 and 2016 (what Colorado is doing)
 • Run SGP analyses with an additional dummy variable indicating mode (crossing 2015 and
 2016).
